brightness.note: Only the sun and fixed hours move the brightness, and only when they turn the day over. Night never raises it and day never lowers it, so a screen you turned down yourself stays where you put it.
brightness.title: BRIGHTNESS
brightness.undrivenNote: Displays that cannot be driven are not listed. A monitor with no DDC, or one whose firmware refuses, is left alone rather than reported broken.
footer.adopt: A theme picked anywhere else lands in the half of the day that is running.
mode.pinnedNote: Pinned. The theme is not following the schedule; switch to Auto to hand it back.
mode.title: MODE
nightlight.guide: %1 K is %2. 6500 K is neutral, 5000 barely shows, 4000 is comfortable for an evening, below 3000 most people find too much. The change is spread over the whole window, so no single minute of it is visible.
nightlight.note.auto: Follows the day on its own — pinning a theme does not stop it.
nightlight.note.held: Held where you put it until the day next turns over.
nightlight.note.off: Omarchy's own toggle is left to behave exactly as it always has.
nightlight.note.on: Held warm around the clock, whatever the day is doing.
nightlight.sharedNote: Shares the night light with Omarchy's own toggle: switching it on there hands the schedule the wheel, switching it off takes it back.
nightlight.title: NIGHT LIGHT
note.off: The plugin is off, so nothing moves this.
note.pinned: A half is pinned, so the schedule is not running and this does not move. Switch back to Auto and it lands on the half of the day that is running, without waiting for the next turn.
note.sensor: The light sensor says whether the room is dark, not when it will turn. With no turn to move on, this stays where you leave it.
schedule.needsLocation:
Sunrise and sunset need a location. Set one in the Weather widget, or run:
omarchy-weather-location --set "City" lat,lon
schedule.pinnedNote: Pinned, so the schedule is not running: nothing here moves the theme, the brightness or the volume until Auto takes over. The night light keeps going, because it has hours of its own.
schedule.title: SCHEDULE
sensor.explanation: Above %1 is day, below is night. Currently %2.
sensor.noThreshold: No threshold set, so the sun or fixed hours are running instead. Cover the sensor until it reads dark, then press Set from now.
sensor.pending: Reading suggests %1; holding until it stays there.
sensor.switchNote: Sensors read differently from one another, so check the threshold after switching between them.
sensor.undecided: Undecided — the reading sits inside the neutral band.
slot.undecodable: This wallpaper is in a format Qt cannot decode here, so the desktop paints black behind a transparent bar. Transparency is held off until it can render; the preference above is kept.
volume.note: Only the sun and fixed hours move the volume, and only when they turn the day over — not when you pin a half yourself. Night never raises it and day never lowers it, so a machine you deliberately hushed stays hushed. Reach for the volume mid-fade and the fade gives way.
volume.title: VOLUME
